title: Let Us Join, ('Tis God Commands)
description: Let Us Join, ('Tis God Commands) in Tonic Solfa to HOLLINGSIDE, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Wesley printed these words in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 521. They first appeared in a book he and his brother Charles published together, and the Collection's own index cannot say which of the two wrote them.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Sevens Double (7.7.7.7.7.7.7.7), and this page sets them to HOLLINGSIDE; any other Sevens Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: Let us join, ('tis God com-mands) Let us join our hearts and hands Help to gain our call-ing's hope, Build we each the oth-er up: God his bless-ings shall dis-pense, God shall crown his or-di-nance; Meet in his ap-point-ed ways; Nour-ish us with so-cial grace.

lines: Let us join our hearts and hands
Help to gain our calling's hope,
Build we each the other up:
Let us then as brethren love,
Follow Christ in heart and mind,
Plead we thus for faith alone,
Faith which by our works is shown:
Conquers earth, and hell, and sin,
Forms the Saviour in the soul.
Let us for this faith contend,
Till we see our Lord appear,
Saved by faith, which works by love.

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788; John Wesley died in 1791.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788) or John Wesley (1703–1791), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to HOLLINGSIDE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
